argv:
Rewrite the text in the manner of Ernest Hemingway's prose.

Use short declarative sentences. Join them with "and" more often than with
subordinating conjunctions. Use concrete nouns and plain verbs. Name things
rather than describing them.

Cut adjectives and adverbs to almost nothing. State actions and facts without
interpreting them. Let the emotion sit under the surface of the sentence
rather than on top of it. Repeat a plain word rather than reaching for a
synonym.

Do not imitate any specific published passage.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
It is interesting to contemplate an entangled bank, clothed with many plants of many kinds, with birds singing on the bushes, with various insects flitting about, and with worms crawling through the damp earth, and to reflect that these elaborately constructed forms, so different from each other, and dependent on each other in so complex a manner, have all been produced by laws acting around us. These laws, taken in the largest sense, being Growth with Reproduction; Inheritance which is almost implied by reproduction; Variability from the indirect and direct action of the external conditions of life, and from use and disuse; a Ratio of Increase so high as to lead to a Struggle for Life, and as a consequence to Natural Selection, entailing Divergence of Character and the Extinction of less-improved forms. Thus, from the war of nature, from famine and death, the most exalted object which we are capable of conceiving, namely, the production of the higher animals, directly follows. There is grandeur in this view of life, with its several powers, having been originally breathed into a few forms or into one; and that, whilst this planet has gone cycling on according to the fixed law of gravity, from so simple a beginning endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved.
</passage>

response.text:
Look at the bank. It is tangled and green with plants of many kinds. Birds sing in the bushes. Insects move through the air. Worms crawl in the wet earth. Each form is built a certain way and each is different from the rest. Each depends on the others in ways that run deep. And laws made them, laws that work around us now.

The laws are these. Growth. Reproduction. Inheritance, which comes near enough with reproduction. Variation, born from the world pressing on life, direct and indirect, and from use and from disuse. A rate of increase so high it makes a struggle for life. And from that struggle comes Natural Selection. And from Selection comes the branching-out of forms, and the death of the forms not fit.

So out of war, out of famine, out of death, comes the thing we hold highest — the higher animals, made. This is what follows. Follows straight.

There is a grandeur in it. Life, with its powers, breathed first into one form or into a few. And the earth has turned all this time on its fixed law of gravity. And from a start so plain there have come, and there keep coming, forms without end, and each one beautiful, and each one a wonder.
